title: Terrain
coreMove: Match the decision to the ground and to your own condition before blaming fate or the opponent.
sourcePressure: The source classifies six kinds of terrain and six calamities caused by the general, then insists that enemy openness, your own readiness, and the nature of the ground all have to align.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating terrain as external circumstances only, with no responsibility for command failures.

sourceAnchors.name: six kinds of terrain
sourceAnchors.detail: Accessible, entangling, temporizing, narrow passes, precipitous heights, and distant positions each call for different action.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The same courage becomes foolishness on the wrong ground.

sourceAnchors.name: six calamities of command
sourceAnchors.detail: Flight, insubordination, collapse, ruin, disorganization, and rout are described as faults the general is responsible for, not natural causes.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Some defeats arrive wearing the costume of bad luck, but the orders made them possible.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
examples: manager staring at a spreadsheet with a coffee cup

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches repeated phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes six examples feel like one example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a direct question, a tactical aside, a second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence

exampleSpecs.domain: regional hospital moving a specialty clinic to a smaller building
exampleSpecs.audience: service director balancing access and staffing
exampleSpecs.stakes: a cheap lease could trap patients and staff in a bad flow
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The new clinic corridor narrows at the elevator while Olivia maps patient volume, wheelchair turns, staff authority, and return paths before signing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a narrow clinic corridor by an elevator

exampleSpecs.domain: construction foreman deciding whether to pour concrete before rain
exampleSpecs.audience: site foreman managing a bridge repair
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rushed pour on bad ground wastes materials and delays traffic reopening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Wet aggregate clings to Jack's boot as he rejects the pour because access, weather, crew readiness, and cure time do not align.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet aggregate on a work boot

exampleSpecs.domain: publisher choosing a launch date against a dominant bestseller
exampleSpecs.audience: marketing director for a nonfiction release
exampleSpecs.stakes: launching into occupied attention could bury the book
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Is this open ground, or are you trying to climb a height already held by someone else?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bookstore front table already reserved

exampleSpecs.domain: regional police unit assigning roles during a major public protest
exampleSpecs.stakes: unclear duties could turn crowd control into disorganization
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 5:45 a.m., Anke redraws sector duties when she sees senior officers bunched together and new constables exposed at the narrow exit.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated sector map under a streetlamp

exampleSpecs.domain: marine salvage crew deciding whether to board a listing cargo ship
exampleSpecs.stakes: the ship can be saved only if the boarding path is not a trap
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Catarina circle once more instead of boarding from pride, because the ladder angle and swell turn access into entangling ground.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ladder slapping against a listing hull

exampleSpecs.domain: food manufacturer handling a contamination test at a satellite plant
exampleSpecs.stakes: partial knowledge could trigger a wrong shutdown or miss a real threat
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Aman one unnecessary shutdown to learn that knowing the product risk but not the plant layout was only halfway to victory.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sealed sample bags in a foam shipper

skillTargets: separate natural difficulty from command-caused calamity
require self, enemy, and ground to align

tryThisNowSpec: Classify one decision as open, entangling, narrow, high, distant, or waiting ground, then ask what command failure would make it worse.
